chapters.subject: Science
chapters.chapterTitle: Mindful Eating: A Path to a Healthy Body
chapters.textbookRef: Curiosity – Grade 6 Science (NCERT) • Chapter 3: Mindful Eating: A Path to a Healthy Body
chapters.overview: Understand major nutrients (carbohydrates, fats, proteins, vitamins, minerals, dietary fibre, water), deficiency diseases, balanced diet, millets, and food miles with complete NCERT textbook exercises.
keyPoints: Carbohydrates and fats are energy-giving foods; fats provide more energy per gram than carbohydrates.
Proteins are body-building foods essential for growth and repair of tissues.
Vitamins and minerals are protective foods needed in small quantities to prevent deficiency diseases.
Iodine test turns starch blue-black; Copper sulphate + caustic soda turns protein violet; Oily translucent patch on paper indicates fats.
formulasAndRules: Starch Test: Food + Iodine solution → Blue-Black colour
Protein Test: Food paste + Copper sulphate + Caustic soda → Violet colour
Fat Test: Crushed food on paper → Oily translucent patch
Balanced Diet = Right proportions of Carbohydrates, Fats, Proteins, Vitamins, Minerals, Roughage & Water

solvedExamples.prompt: A student has bleeding gums and slow-healing wounds. Identify the likely missing vitamin and suggest two food sources.
solvedExamples.solution:
Deficiency Disease: Scurvy.
Missing Nutrient: Vitamin C.
Recommended Food Sources: Amla (Indian gooseberry), oranges, lemons, guava, tomatoes.

textbookExerciseSolutions.question: Pick the odd one out and give reasons: (i) Jowar, Bajra, Ragi, Chana  (ii) Kidney beans, Green gram, Soya bean, Rice
textbookExerciseSolutions.conceptUsed: Classification of Millets vs Pulses vs Cereals
textbookExerciseSolutions.answer:
(i) Odd one out: Chana — Jowar, Bajra, and Ragi are millets (nutri-cereals), whereas Chana (chickpea) is a pulse.
(ii) Odd one out: Rice — Kidney beans, green gram, and soya bean are protein-rich pulses, whereas Rice is a carbohydrate-rich cereal.
textbookExerciseSolutions.stepByStepExplanation: Group foods by botanical type and primary nutrient: Millets/Cereals supply energy-rich carbohydrates, while pulses/legumes supply body-building proteins.

textbookExerciseSolutions.question: Discuss traditional versus modern culinary practices in India.
textbookExerciseSolutions.conceptUsed: Evolution of Cooking Equipment & Nutrition Retention
textbookExerciseSolutions.answer:
1. Traditional practices used clay chulhas, sil-batta (stone grinders), and slow cooking in earthen pots, preserving dietary fibre and local seasonal grains.
2. Modern practices use gas stoves, induction cooktops, electric mixers, and packaged/ultra-processed foods that save time but often strip fibre and add excess sugar/salt.
textbookExerciseSolutions.stepByStepExplanation: Compare cooking heat source, grinding tools, ingredient freshness, and nutritional retention side by side.

textbookExerciseSolutions.typeLabel: Why Junk Food Alone Cannot Keep Us Healthy
textbookExerciseSolutions.question: A teacher says that good nutrition is needed along with regular exercise. Why are burgers, chips, and sugary soft drinks not a balanced diet even if eaten in large amounts?
textbookExerciseSolutions.answer: Junk foods contain excess refined sugar, salt, and unhealthy fats with very high calories, but lack proteins, vitamins, minerals, and dietary fibre. Eating them regularly causes obesity and nutrient deficiencies.
textbookExerciseSolutions.stepByStepExplanation: A balanced diet depends on nutrient completeness across all food groups, not calorie quantity alone.

textbookExerciseSolutions.question: Match the deficient vitamin/mineral with its disorder: (1) Vitamin A  (2) Vitamin B₁  (3) Vitamin C  (4) Vitamin D  (5) Iodine  (6) Iron ↔ (a) Anaemia  (b) Goitre  (c) Rickets  (d) Loss of vision  (e) Scurvy  (f) Beriberi
textbookExerciseSolutions.answer: 1 → (d) Loss of vision | 2 → (f) Beriberi | 3 → (e) Scurvy | 4 → (c) Rickets | 5 → (b) Goitre | 6 → (a) Anaemia
textbookExerciseSolutions.stepByStepExplanation:
• Vitamin A supports eye health (deficiency → night blindness).
• Vitamin B₁ → Beriberi.
• Vitamin C → Scurvy.
• Vitamin D helps calcium absorption for bones → Rickets.
• Iodine → Goitre (swollen neck gland).
• Iron builds haemoglobin → Anaemia.

textbookExerciseSolutions.question:
(a) __________ is a rich source of dietary fibre and helps remove undigested food from our body.
(b) The distance travelled by a food item from farm to consumer is called __________.
(c) Millets are known as __________ because they are rich in vitamins, minerals, and fibre.
textbookExerciseSolutions.stepByStepExplanation: All three terms are directly defined in NCERT Curiosity Grade 6 Chapter 3.

classNotebookExercises.prompt: Define Nutrients, Balanced Diet, and Food Miles.
classNotebookExercises.modelAnswer: Nutrients: Essential chemical components in food needed for energy, growth, and protection. Balanced Diet: A meal containing all nutrients, roughage, and water in right amounts. Food Miles: Total distance food travels from producer to plate.

classNotebookExercises.prompt: Prepare a table for Starch, Protein, and Fat food tests showing reagent used and positive colour/result.
classNotebookExercises.modelAnswer: Starch: Iodine → Blue-black; Protein: CuSO₄ + NaOH → Violet; Fat: Paper crush → Translucent oily patch.

classNotebookExercises.prompt: Write deficiency diseases, symptoms, and food sources for Vitamin A, Vitamin C, Vitamin D, Iron, and Iodine.
classNotebookExercises.modelAnswer: Vit A: Night blindness (carrots); Vit C: Scurvy (amla); Vit D: Rickets (sunlight, milk); Iron: Anaemia (spinach); Iodine: Goitre (iodised salt).

classNotebookExercises.prompt: Roughage provides no energy or nutrients, yet it is essential in our diet. Give reasons.
classNotebookExercises.modelAnswer: Roughage adds bulk to food and helps our body easily eliminate undigested solid waste, preventing constipation.

classNotebookExercises.prompt: Why should vegetables and fruits be washed before peeling/cutting rather than after?
classNotebookExercises.modelAnswer: Washing after cutting washes away water-soluble vitamins (like Vitamin B and C) and minerals from the exposed surfaces.

classNotebookExercises.prompt: State the main function and two sources each for Carbohydrates, Fats, and Proteins.
classNotebookExercises.modelAnswer: Carbs: Quick energy (rice, wheat); Fats: Stored energy (ghee, nuts); Proteins: Growth/repair (dal, eggs).

classNotebookExercises.prompt: State True or False: (a) By eating rice alone, we can fulfil all nutritional needs. (b) Eating local seasonal food reduces food miles.
classNotebookExercises.modelAnswer: (a) False — rice lacks proteins and all vitamins. (b) True.

classNotebookExercises.prompt: Name any four Indian millets and state two benefits of eating them.
classNotebookExercises.modelAnswer: Jowar, Bajra, Ragi, Sanwa (Barnyard millet). They are rich in minerals, dietary fibre, and grow well in varied climates.

classNotebookExercises.prompt: Design a balanced Indian lunch plate containing all five nutrient groups plus roughage and water.
classNotebookExercises.writingGuidance: Label each food item with its primary nutrient.
classNotebookExercises.modelAnswer: Roti/Rice (Carbs) + Dal/Paneer (Protein) + Ghee (Fat) + Spinach/Carrot Sabzi (Vitamins/Minerals) + Cucumber Salad (Roughage) + Water.

classNotebookExercises.prompt: What does the '+F' symbol on packaged food labels like milk, oil, or salt indicate?
classNotebookExercises.modelAnswer: The '+F' logo shows that the food has been fortified with extra essential vitamins or minerals (such as iodine in salt or Vitamins A & D in milk).
